title: Canary Simulator & Operator Cheatsheet (wip)
content:
Purpose:
Quick operator-facing reference for running simulation-led canaries using the local simulator and Redwood traffic controls. This is a living cheat sheet: lightweight, step-focused, and intentionally *actionable* (not theoretical).

Scope and intent:
- For SREs, release stewards, and product stewards who run canaries and micro-experiments for latency-sensitive LLM features.
- Emphasis on pre-flight checks, synthetic traffic scenarios, stop conditions, rollback actions, and concise comms templates.
- Not a replacement for the full runbook; this is the fast path when time is limited.

Pre-flight checklist (10 min):
- Confirm experiment config in Console: model, route, rollout percent, abort thresholds.
- Validate linked evaluation set exists and is the latest commit id. If stale -> tag: NEED-EVAL-UPDATE.
- Ensure canary synthetic generator is on the right template (see Payload Matrix).
- Verify observability dashboards are loaded and time-window set to last 15m. Key panels: p50/p95 latency, token-rate, error-rate (4xx/5xx), hallucination score (eval probe), cost burn rate.
- Notify oncall and stakeholders via #rollouts channel with one-line: who / what / window / abort-criteria.

Quick simulator commands (local devbox with access):
- Start simulator: ./canary-sim --config ./configs/sample-latency-heavy.yaml --api-key $REDWOOD_KEY
- Kick a 5-minute smoke: ./canary-sim --profile smoke-5m --target-route /v1/chat --qps 2
- Ramp sequence (example): ./canary-sim --sequence ramp-0-10pct-30m.yaml
- Cancel: ctrl-c (graceful) or ./canary-sim --shutdown <run-id>
- Emit single synthetic event (for manual probes): curl -X POST $SIM_ENDPOINT -d '{"prompt":"<smoke-probe>","meta":{"user":"synthetic-canary"}}'

Payload Matrix (pick one):
- latency-stress: longer contexts (>=1024 tokens), long generation, rare tokens -> surface kernel/kv-cache regressions.
- semantic-regression: eval prompts from curated eval set (diff expectation checks).
- safety-probe: adversarially phrased prompts to surface guardrail failures.
- spike-pattern: bursty QPS (e.g., 20 rps for 60s) to validate autoscale and circuit-breakers.

Core stop conditions (auto + manual):
Auto-abort (system):
- 5-minute rolling error-rate >= 2% AND increase > 3x baseline -> immediate abort.
- p95 latency > latency SLO + 300ms for 3 consecutive windows (1m windows) -> auto abort.
- Model quality regression: automated eval score drop >= 5% on the groomed eval set -> suspend.

Manual triggers for abort (human):
- Unexpected hallucination class flagged by product owner (Slack ping + /abort).
- Customer-facing anomalies called out by CS (immediate rollback).
- Cost burn above expected threshold (alert + investigation).

Rollback matrix (fast options):
- 1) Route fallback to baseline model (recommended for most). Command: POST /api/rollouts/fallback {"route":"/v1/chat","target":"model:baseline-v3"}
- 2) Throttle traffic: reduce canary weight to 0.5% for quick mitigation while we triage.
- 3) Pause feature at edge (feature-flag off) when human-in-loop required.
- 4) Hotfix: apply prompt-safety shim in the routing layer (temporary prefix) if hallucination pattern is prompt-hacked.

Observation checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Confirm synthetic probes are arriving and being served (sim logs show requests and successful responses).
- p50 stable, p95 trending — if both jump, suspect kernel/hotpath.
- Token throughput: compare to expected per-second token rate; wide variance -> batching mismatch.
- Failures: sample 5 failed requests and paste traces to incident thread.
- Quality probes: run 20 eval queries, check top-3 diffs; if >=4 diffs, start investigation.

Example anomaly notes to paste in Slack/Incident: (short form)
- [10:13] Canary run sim-231: p95 latency spiked from 220ms -> 840ms, errors 1.8% -> 4.6% concurrent with spike-pattern step. Sampling shows attention-kernel OOM in node kube-12. Rolling fallback started.

Comms templates (use in #rollouts):
- Start: "START: canary sim-231 | route=/v1/chat | profile=latency-stress | window=20m | owner=@PriyaNair | abort-criteria=auto p95>+300ms OR errors>2%"
- Abort: "ABORT: canary sim-231 | reason=p95-latency >> SLO | action=fallback->baseline-v3 | rollback by @EthanWalker | notes: see incident thread <link>"
- Pause/Investigate: "PAUSE: canary sim-231 | action=throttle -> 0.5% | oncall @MayaPatel triaging traces"

Post-mortem quick template (fill in after run):
- Run id:
- Start/stop time:
- Profile used:
- Trigger (auto/manual):
- Short timeline (5 bullets):
- Mitigation taken:
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Action items (owners + due dates):

Operator heuristics & tips (collected):
- When p95 and error-rate both increase but p50 stays low, suspect contagion from batching/queue saturation rather than model slowdown.
- If only semantic evals fail (quality) but infra looks fine -> revert model weights or apply prompt-mitigation.
- Use a small human-verified probe set for immediate quality triage (10 queries).
- Prefer route fallback over full rollback when customer impact is limited; preserves capacity and reduces churn.

Mini-scenarios (run these when practicing):
1) Burst-failure: ramp to 25rps for 2m, then drop to 1rps. Expected: autoscaler adds nodes within 60s, p95 should not exceed 500ms. Failure: scale lag -> errors spike.
2) Quality drift: run semantic-regression profile with new quantized model at 5% traffic for 30m. Expected: eval drop <2%. Failure: revert immediately.
3) Mixed-failure: latency + quality degrade together — likely model/hardware mismatch; fallback to smaller model class and open incident.

Sample routing policy JSON (paste to APIs or Console advanced):
{
  "route": "/v1/chat",
  "variants": [
    {"id":"canary-a","model":"gptq-7b-q4_0","weight":5},
    {"id":"baseline","model":"baseline-v3","weight":95}
  ],
  "fallback_policy": {"on_errors_percent":2, "switch_to":"baseline"},
  "telemetry_checkpoint": ["p95_latency","error_rate","eval_regression"]
}

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a short JSON -> Console import template so stewards can paste policies faster (owner: Jonas Richter).
- Add automatic post-run diff report in Slack (owner: Ethan Walker).
- Flesh out a dedicated low-latency practice sandbox with smaller quotas for rehearsal.

Related tickets / references:
- JIRA-REQ-4821: Canary simulator infra improvements
- Confluence: CI-Canary-Sim (detailed design)
- github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim (scripts + profiles)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc crisp. When we land the console import, replace many of the manual commands with a single-run button flow.
- When in doubt during a live run: throttle -> sample -> fallback.
